```{r}
#| include: false
source("code/setup.R")
library(knitr)
analysis <- readRDS("results/analysis.rds")
tab1 <- readRDS("results/table1.rds")
models <- readRDS("results/models.rds")
eff <- models$effects
```

The report does no computing of its own. It reads the objects the pipeline
produced and displays them, so that rendering it can never quietly change a
result.

## Analysis set

`r nrow(analysis)` participants had a week 12 measurement:
`r sum(analysis$arm == "Placebo")` on placebo and
`r sum(analysis$arm == "Treatment")` on treatment.

## Table 1

```{r}
kable(tab1, col.names = c("Characteristic",
                          sprintf("Placebo (n = %d)", attr(tab1, "n")[["Placebo"]]),
                          sprintf("Treatment (n = %d)", attr(tab1, "n")[["Treatment"]])),
      align = "lcc")
```

## Change in FEV1

![](results/figure1.png)

## Treatment effect

```{r}
kable(eff, digits = 3, col.names = c("Model", "Estimate", "Lower", "Upper", "p", "n"),
      align = "lccccc")
```

The estimated treatment effect is
`r sprintf("%.3f L (95%% CI %.3f to %.3f)", eff$estimate[eff$model == "adjusted"], eff$lower[eff$model == "adjusted"], eff$upper[eff$model == "adjusted"])`
in the adjusted model, and is insensitive to which covariates are included.
